files.README.md:
# Animation scheduling

This existing example uses public scheduled previews. WidgetKit controls system refresh and can freeze motion; the app/Web preview is not a guarantee of continuous Home Screen animation. Mac, inactive scenes and accessibility modes have static fallbacks. Custom clock periods are signed half-turn durations. Source is preserved; use native date/text components when accurate continuously updating digital time is needed. See docs/public-animations.md in the repository for compatibility details.

# Responsive composition

Each creature has its own fixed-size cell; spaces are not used for positioning. Small widgets use fewer creatures, large and extra-large widgets add a swimming row, and lock-screen accessories use compact static compositions. Swing distances stay small so fish and bubbles remain within the scene. Edit the `Row` symbol arrays to customize it; this dynamic template is edited in Code. Existing user copies are not overwritten.

templates.name: Control Switch
templates.description: One persistent local switch shared by widgets, Control Center and Shortcuts. This does not change a system setting.

files.README.md:
# Control Switch

Install this package to get one local persistent flag, `switch.enabled`. It is not a system Focus mode, network appliance or device setting. It requests storage only. The widget Toggle, the ScriptWidget control-center toggle and Shortcuts use the same declared action and package installation identity.

In Shortcuts, select **Run ScriptWidget Action**, then Toggle local switch, Turn local switch on, or Turn local switch off. In Control Center, add a ScriptWidget toggle and choose Local switch from this installation. Explicit toggle values are idempotent: setting true twice stays true rather than toggling twice. Writes use bounded compare-and-set retries. Actions request ordinary widget and compatible control reloads; the system decides when to render them.

Rendering never writes a fake initial value. An unset flag displays Off. The flag survives reopening with the same installed package, is isolated from other installations and is not inherited by deleting/reinstalling the same name. Read-only template previews cannot execute actions. The bundled On preview uses a synthetic isolated fixture.

This developer example does not use the native daily-record backup format. Exporting the script package exports code, not its local storage flag. Use an explicit data-export feature in a project if the flag needs a portable backup. Widget interactivity, Control Center availability, Shortcuts discovery and real cross-process execution still require appropriate OS versions and signed-device acceptance.

templates.name: Countdown
templates.description: A calm countdown with saved dates, yearly repeats and three accent colors. Configure it in Records & Configuration or use a date parameter.

files.README.md:
# Countdown

Install the complete template, then open **Records & Configuration** from the installed widget's menu. Choose an event name, a target date, whether it repeats every year, and a blue, rose or green accent. Save Configuration publishes the settings for that installation. Backup & Restore includes these settings; the countdown does not invent daily history or check-ins.

An empty parameter uses the saved configuration. Before choosing a date the widget shows a setup prompt. Each widget instance may override the saved settings:

- `2027-07-12 Summer trip` counts local Gregorian calendar days.
- `2027-07-12T12:30:00 Flight` keeps the earlier local-time countdown format, including counting up after the moment.
- `{"title":"Birthday","targetDate":"2024-02-29","repeatYearly":true,"accent":"rose"}` repeats February 29 only in leap years.

JSON overrides may contain `title`, `targetDate`, `repeatYearly` and `accent` only. Dates must be real calendar dates in `YYYY-MM-DD` form from 1970 through 9999. Names accept up to 40 UTF-16 code units; the small widget shortens the visible title. Past dates show days since, and the target day shows Today. Parameters override rendering without modifying saved configuration.

Calendar days use date ordinals rather than elapsed 24-hour periods, so daylight-saving changes do not shift the result. Date-only input is kept as a local calendar date rather than parsed as UTC. A local timestamp that falls inside a daylight-saving gap is rejected. Yearly repeats ignore the original year, but preserve the selected month and day. The next valid February 29 is chosen rather than moving the event to March 1.

All declared home-screen and accessory families render offline. The package requests storage only. Midnight timeline entries allow the date to advance; WidgetKit decides when to display updates. This is not a continuously ticking or exact-alarm timer. Records stay on this installation/device; the template does not promise record synchronization through iCloud.

# GitHub Profile

Install this template, then open ScriptWidget Settings > Service Accounts. Connect a GitHub personal access token and allow this installed widget to read the account profile. Reconnecting clears widget grants; deleting and reinstalling the widget creates a new identity and requires a new grant. No token belongs in the script, manifest, parameters or Web Studio mocks.

The template reads `$services.status("github")` and `$services.profile("github")`. It displays repository/follower counts, preserves an unshared private repository count as missing, and shows setup, expiry, rate-limit and offline states. A zero count is real data, not an error. It does not store profile data, send mutations or perform a login. Future entries and Live Activity presentations cannot query live services; prepare the display data in the current execution before composing such presentations.

Web Studio starts with a healthy sample profile. Connected Services mocks let you edit names/counts and simulate missing authorization, disconnection, expiry, rate limits or offline behavior. These samples do not connect a real account. See [Services API](../../../../../../docs/services-api.md).

templates.description: Stars, forks and issues for any GitHub repository.

files.README.md:
# Public repository stats

Save a public `owner/repository` and accent in Records & Configuration. The legacy `owner/repository` instance parameter is supported; JSON may override `repository` and `accent` (`blue`, `green`, `rose`). URLs, credentials and unknown settings are rejected. The package declares only `api.github.com` network access and local storage.

This template uses GitHub's public REST API without credentials. Anonymous requests share an IP-based rate limit. It uses at least a one-hour cache, conditional Last-Modified requests where supplied and retry backoff. HTTP 403/429 shows a rate-limit state, not invented zeros. A missing/deleted/private repository (404) discards its old displayed counts. Invalid bodies, unexpected repository names, private payloads and invalid counts are never accepted as current data.

Offline cached values are labelled with the time last received or validated; counts older than seven days are unavailable. The cache holds at most four repositories. Daily star history is created only from successful payloads, using UTC day buckets, replacing the latest check on the same day and retaining fourteen recorded days. Missing days are not filled. The graph appears after two recorded days; its categories are actual check dates. It is not a reconstruction of historical GitHub counts. GitHub's `open_issues_count` includes issues and pull requests, so the card labels it “Issues + PRs”.

The template never requests an access token. Private repositories and authenticated services require a separate native credential capability, not a token pasted into this package. Record backups contain configuration only; transient counts and their history are excluded. Future timeline entries may display the cache but cannot request data or modify storage. Widget refresh remains system scheduled.

Web Studio defaults and the bundled preview contain explicitly synthetic sample counts. They do not claim the real repository has these counts.

GitHub guidance: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/best-practices-for-using-the-rest-api and https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api. Conditional requests are not universally free of rate limits; do not infer an authenticated quota from this anonymous template.

# Health Overview

files.README.md:
# Health card

Install the complete package, then open Records & Configuration to choose steps, active energy or latest heart rate. Save a daily step goal and active-energy goal. An optional JSON instance parameter overrides `metric` (`steps`, `energy`, `heart`), `stepsGoal` (1–100000) or `energyGoal` (1–10000 kcal).

On iPhone, enable Health access from ScriptWidget Settings. The script never prompts for authorization or writes to HealthKit. It queries only the chosen metric in the current timeline entry. Other platforms, uninstalled native previews and future projections show guidance instead of reading personal data. Web Studio uses editable, explicitly simulated examples.

HealthKit does not reveal whether read access was denied. No readable samples, including a legacy zero without sample-presence information, show an explanatory empty state. API 1.3 adds `hasSamples`; a readable zero is valid for steps/energy. This flag indicates readable data presence, never permission status. See Apple's authorization documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/healthkit/authorizing-access-to-health-data.

Daily totals use the device's current day and are accepted only with a recent query timestamp. Heart rate is the latest available sample, labelled with its age, never a live measurement or a goal ring; samples older than 24 hours are not shown. Invalid units, dates and values are rejected. Refresh timing is controlled by the system.

Health readings are not persisted by this template. Record backups contain configuration only. WidgetKit may retain an already-rendered view until it next refreshes; this template cannot promise immediate system refresh after permissions change. Bundled artwork and test previews use synthetic readings, never private data.

templates.name: Hydration Goal iCloud
templates.description: An opt-in iCloud hydration example with timestamped taps and additive offline merging. Limited by the iCloud JSON revision budget.

files.README.md:
# Hydration Goal iCloud

This is a separate, opt-in iCloud example. It does not change or migrate records from **Hydration Goal**. Install the complete package, then open its **iCloud Data** menu in My Widgets and create a data store. On another device, install the same package and connect it to the **same store ID**. Both devices need a ScriptWidget build supporting Runtime 1.5 and the same iCloud account. Use the widget's **Sync** button or the app's **Sync Now** control to request an exchange; iCloud delivery and WidgetKit refresh can be delayed.

Each **+ glass** tap saves an immutable, timestamped event in `hydration.json` under `iCloud Drive/ScriptWidget/WidgetData/<store ID>/`. The `at` field records the device clock in UTC and `day` is the recording device's local calendar day. The widget derives its daily total and seven-day history from those events. If two devices add glasses while offline, a later user action unions events by ID and resolves the observed fork. Normal rendering only reads cached data; it never writes or claims that another device has received a change. The optional widget parameter is `{"goal":8,"glassML":250}`.

This example is **add-only**. It intentionally has no Reset or Undo: deleting or reversing an event across offline devices needs a separate conflict policy. The existing native **Records & Configuration** backup does not cover this cloud document. Existing local hydration history is not imported, and old daily totals cannot be turned into individual tap times. Do not edit or delete revision files directly; copy them if you need a personal archive.

The current iCloud JSON store is bounded to 256 immutable revisions and 2 MiB across all documents, with no automatic compaction. Every tap and conflict resolution consumes a revision. When it reaches the limit, new writes fail while existing revisions remain. This is a bounded example, not an unlimited long-term health log. Before using it for sustained tracking, export an archive and use a future record-sync capability with a retention/compaction design.

files.README.md:
# Layout Starter

Copy this template into a project and open **Layout** above the code editor. Select a layer in the tree or select its JSX in Code. Edit text or choose a property and Apply. Drag a layer before another layer, use Move up/down, or select a container and Move inside. The stack/grid must contain literal JSX children; dynamic expressions remain in Code. Add text, stack, spacer and icon are available on supported containers.

Changes update the normal source file and preview. Undo and Redo share the editor history. The exported package includes your JSX, rather than an extra visual layout file. No-op opening/export preserves source text exactly. The template declares the five system widget families; accessory layouts require a separately designed compact composition.

All values here are literal and editable. Introduce variables or dynamic expressions in Code whenever you need them. Layout preserves those expressions and displays its editing boundary. It does not evaluate JavaScript, request system permission or replace unsupported source.

Open **Theme** and choose **Connect layout to Meadow theme** to bind literal styles to reusable tokens. Apply a palette, adjust individual fonts/spacing/colors, or copy/import version 1 theme JSON. Open **Assets** to select a literal container and insert original Bloom/Leaf marks or a static Pebble friend. Original art follows a connected theme and retains its MIT source/license in exported JSX. To add a photo, use the existing image import tools, then select a supported image from the package's `image/` directory in Assets. These commands share the normal save/preview and Undo history. The separate Pocket Pet template supplies persistent care interactions.

files.README.md:
# Weather forecast

Open **Records & Configuration** to save a city, latitude/longitude and Celsius or Fahrenheit. City search uses Apple Maps; you can also enter coordinates directly. On iPhone, optionally enable current location. If location is unavailable, the saved city is used. The script never requests permission itself.

Weather is a forecast from MET Norway, not a live observation. Requests send coordinates rounded to two decimal places to api.met.no. See https://api.met.no/doc/TermsOfService and https://api.met.no/doc/License. Weather data: MET Norway, CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Icons use system SF Symbols, not the provider’s artwork.

The bounded local cache keeps at most four places (at most one current-location entry). Expiry and conditional requests follow response headers, with a minimum refresh interval and retry backoff. Cached forecasts show their source age and refresh failures. Data older than 24 hours or without a nearby forecast point is unavailable; temperatures are never invented. Future timeline projections do not fetch or change storage. System scheduling can delay refresh.

A record backup contains saved configuration only; transient forecast/location cache is excluded. Exporting the script package and exporting records are separate operations.

Optional instance parameter: `latitude,longitude,City`, or a JSON object containing `city`, `latitude`, `longitude`, `useLocation`, and/or `unit` (`c` or `f`). Instance parameters override saved settings.

Web Studio shows editable synthetic Mock responses, not current weather. The bundled preview is an explicitly synthetic native-rendered example.

# Material Study

Original geometric shapes sit behind a public SwiftUI frosted material card. A small fixed 3D tilt adds depth to the backdrop while keeping the text sharp; this is a static composition, not device-motion parallax. Change the literal `backgroundMaterial` property in Layout to compare ultraThin/thin/regular/thick/ultraThick or none. `background` supplies the color fallback. Runtime API 1.4 is required; no permissions or network are needed.

Reduce Transparency composites the fallback over an opaque base. Reduce Motion removes the 3D tilt. In accented/vibrant rendering the decorative shapes are hidden and local material is omitted, leaving system rendering in charge. Compact accessory families use text only. Web Studio offers matching accessibility preview controls, with a clearly marked CSS approximation of material.

Material blurs content inside the widget. It does not read or blur Home Screen wallpaper. Clear/Tinted system Liquid Glass is a system/user appearance choice. This template uses no private clock-hand/swing effect, continuous animation, wallpaper-setting API or background sensor subscription. Original geometry and source follow the repository MIT license.

# Music Playback

Shows a snapshot of the **iOS Music app**, using `$music.current()` from Runtime API 1.4. Install the widget and allow Music access in ScriptWidget Settings. The package declares `music`; it does not need network access.

Web Studio supplies editable samples. Choose Music playback in Mock Data to simulate playing, paused, stopped, withheld track details, denied permission or an unavailable platform. Samples stay in your browser project and are not exported.

The public system-player API is unavailable on macOS. Other audio apps are outside its scope. Home Sharing can withhold track details even while playback continues. Duration and position can be null. Playback is a snapshot at render time, rather than a continuously running progress display. There are no playback controls, queue changes, artwork requests or library scans in this template.

The native adapter compiles for iOS app and widget targets. Real Music authorization and widget-extension behavior still require signed-device validation; automated native tests use an injected provider and never read your music.

files.README.md:
# Photo Card

Install this template, then open **Records & Configuration** from its menu. Choose a photo from Photos or import an image file. Adjust the crop's zoom and horizontal/vertical position, add the photo, select and reorder your pictures, choose Single/Two/Four-photo layout, then **Save Configuration**. Each installation keeps its own settings. Nothing is imported or saved merely by rendering the template.

Only the selected Photos item is transferred. The template itself cannot browse your photo library, read album identifiers, access the network, or modify the originals. Imported files are read with a 25 MiB bound, thumbnails normalize image orientation, and cropped package assets are at most 768 × 768 pixels. Original GPS and capture-time metadata are discarded; image dimensions and color-space information may be generated by the PNG encoder. Animated inputs use their first frame. Download unavailable iCloud originals before importing.

Keep up to 12 imported assets and select up to four. The configuration screen lets you remove an unused imported photo after confirmation. It does not delete assets referenced by either the saved configuration or your current selection. Missing selected files are identified in the configuration screen so you can reconnect storage or choose replacements.

The small and circular accessories show the first selected image; medium displays the selected layout in one row; large widgets show the collage in rows. Inline accessories show the title. The default widget shows an empty-state guide until you choose photos. A gallery thumbnail uses original code-drawn sample artwork, not personal photos.

The optional per-widget JSON parameter may override `title`, `caption`, `layout` (`single`, `duo` or `grid`) and `photos`. A photo name is the package-local `photo-<UUID>` shown in its settings backup; no URLs, arbitrary paths or cross-package assets are accepted. Titles support 40 UTF-16 code units and captions 80. Native configuration is the recommended way to select photos.

**Backups:** a record backup contains settings and photo references only. Export the complete widget package to include image files. Keep both if you want to restore the layout and pictures on another device. Restoring settings alone can leave missing images; it does not silently insert demo pictures. Records are local to the installation and do not synchronize through iCloud, even when source files are in iCloud Drive.

files.README.md:
# Quick Launcher

Install the complete template. Open Records & Configuration to save a title, accent and one to six ordered links. Each link can be a web URL, an external app URL or the name of a saved Shortcut with optional text input. Add/remove/reorder links, then Save Configuration. Test Draft Link opens the unsaved draft only when you press it.

Web URLs must be absolute HTTP(S), without embedded credentials or spaces. App links require an external URL scheme; script/data/file/internal/settings schemes are not accepted by this template. Installing an app or a matching shortcut is the user's responsibility. Shortcut names and text are encoded as query data so ampersands, plus signs and Unicode cannot introduce extra parameters. It never reads the clipboard, lists shortcuts or executes a shortcut while rendering.

The native test button reports whether the system accepted the URL. Acceptance does not prove that a shortcut or target-app operation completed; confirm in the destination app. Widget links use the system directly. When the containing app receives a forwarded URL, it opens external links and reports missing handlers without logging full URLs. System routing varies by OS/version; the manual device checklist remains required.

Compact and accessory families prioritize the first link, medium shows the first three, and larger families show up to six. Move Up/Down controls which links appear first. The root widget URL falls back to the first item; larger-family link tiles open their individual destinations. The saved title, ordered links and optional shortcut input are included in explicit record backups, so treat those backups as personal data. Total configuration is limited to 32 KiB; links use stable IDs and do not change the package's runtime permissions. This package requests storage only and does not fetch the URL while rendering.

Optional instance parameter: a JSON object overriding `title`, `accent` or the complete `items` list. Each item contains exactly `id`, `title`, `icon`, `type`, `target`, `input`; use the native form for a valid example. Old manually edited launcher projects are not rewritten by this new bundled template.

Apple's Shortcuts URL documentation: https://support.apple.com/guide/shortcuts/apd624386f42/ios and https://support.apple.com/guide/shortcuts-mac/apd624386f42/mac.

files.README.md:
# Reminders Agenda

Shows pending reminders due today from the lists selected in ScriptWidget Settings.

1. Run the installed widget in ScriptWidget and open **Settings → Reminders**.
2. Grant system access, select allowed lists and save.
3. Optionally set the widget parameter to comma-separated IDs from `$reminders.lists()` to narrow the selection further.

The app requires full system Reminders access. The explicit **Complete next** action completes the next due reminder in the selected lists; ordinary rendering only reads. The package declares remindersWrite and storage and keeps a stable pending request until delivery is confirmed. If a result is uncertain, inspect the actual Reminders app first, then use **Checked Reminders? Clear pending** in a medium or larger widget. Clearing the pending request does not undo a system change or erase the runtime write receipt. Undated pending reminders are excluded. Query failures and setup states are shown separately from an empty day. Native execution never inserts sample reminders; Web Studio provides editable samples.

See [Reminders API](../../../../../../../docs/reminders-api.md).

In Web Studio, create a fresh copy of this template and choose **Wallpaper crops…** in the file sidebar. Export the .swt to carry `wallpaper.json` and its cropped images to the native app. Runtime 1.4 or later is required. Existing native saved configuration and preview storage mocks take precedence; imported package defaults never write records automatically. files.README.md:
# Weather forecast

Open **Records & Configuration** to save a city, latitude/longitude and Celsius or Fahrenheit. City search uses Apple Maps; you can also enter coordinates directly. On iPhone, optionally enable current location. If location is unavailable, the saved city is used. The script never requests permission itself.

Weather is a forecast from MET Norway, not a live observation. Requests send coordinates rounded to two decimal places to api.met.no. See https://api.met.no/doc/TermsOfService and https://api.met.no/doc/License. Weather data: MET Norway, CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Icons use system SF Symbols, not the provider’s artwork.

The bounded local cache keeps at most four places (at most one current-location entry). Expiry and conditional requests follow response headers, with a minimum refresh interval and retry backoff. Cached forecasts show their source age and refresh failures. Data older than 24 hours or without a nearby forecast point is unavailable; temperatures are never invented. Future timeline projections do not fetch or change storage. System scheduling can delay refresh.

A record backup contains saved configuration only; transient forecast/location cache is excluded. Exporting the script package and exporting records are separate operations.

Optional instance parameter: `latitude,longitude,City`, or a JSON object containing `city`, `latitude`, `longitude`, `useLocation`, and/or `unit` (`c` or `f`). Instance parameters override saved settings.

Web Studio shows editable synthetic Mock responses, not current weather. The bundled preview is an explicitly synthetic native-rendered example.
